title: Lifts Of Partial Cohomological Field Theories And Examples Of bi-Hamiltonian Structures In The Non-semisimple Case
authors: Guido Carlet, Dimitrios Makris, Sergey Shadrin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define the lift of a partial cohomological field theory with respect to a Frobenius algebra and the corresponding lift of local polyvector fields, extending the lift procedure proposed by Della Vedova, Lorenzoni, and Savoldi. This allows us to systematically produce examples of non-semisimple homogeneous partial cohomological field theories whose integrable systems possess a second Hamiltonian structure, thus confirming the conjecture of Buryak et al. on an explicit formula for the second Poisson bracket in new non-semisimple cases. Moreover we present some relations of these lift constructions with the Morimoto theory of the lift of geometric structures to the Weil bundle of infinitely near points associated to a local algebra.
tldr: This paper defines lifts of partial cohomological field theories and uses them to construct bi-Hamiltonian structures in non-semisimple cases.
motivation: To extend the lift procedure for partial cohomological field theories and confirm a conjecture about explicit formulas for second Poisson brackets in non-semisimple homogeneous cases.
method: The authors define a lift of a partial cohomological field theory with respect to a Frobenius algebra and a corresponding lift of local polyvector fields, building on prior work by Della Vedova, Lorenzoni, and Savoldi.
result: They systematically produce examples of non-semisimple homogeneous partial cohomological field theories whose integrable systems possess a second Hamiltonian structure, confirming the conjecture of Buryak et al.
conclusion: The lift constructions relate to Morimoto's theory of lifts to Weil bundles, providing a systematic method for generating bi-Hamiltonian structures in non-semisimple settings.

title: Field-driven Nonlinear Metasurface: Self-adaptive Transition Between High-selectivity Transmission And Broadband Shielding
authors: Yuan Xu, Hanqing Liu, Shangjing Xi, Xiaodi Zhang, Yanqing Cheng, Wenye Ji, Peiguo Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The escalating complexity of electromagnetic (EM) environment is posing a significant challenge to the reliability of modern electronic information systems. To address the need for the spatial EM safety of electronic devices, we present a field-driven nonlinear metasurface (NMS) that enables effective protection against out-of-band interference and in-band high-intensity radiation. By constructing a reconfigurable hybrid coupling topology and mapping it to the metasurface geometry, the proposed NMS achieves a self-adaptive transition between its transmission and shielding mode depending on the incident power. The experimental results are in good agreement with theoretical analysis and full-wave simulation. We obtain a highly selective passband with roll-off rate larger than 20.6dB/GHz and a broadband shielding with shielding effectiveness exceeding 23.6dB and 60% bandwidth, demonstrating a significantly enhanced performance relative to the literature. Our findings establish a promising route toward comprehensive EM protection on radio frequency front-end systems.
tldr: A field-driven nonlinear metasurface for adaptive electromagnetic shielding and transmission.
motivation: To protect electronic systems from complex electromagnetic interference by enabling self-adaptive switching between high-selectivity transmission and broadband shielding.
method: A reconfigurable hybrid coupling topology is mapped to a metasurface geometry, enabling power-dependent mode transition.
result: Achieves roll-off rate >20.6 dB/GHz in passband and shielding effectiveness >23.6 dB over 60% bandwidth.
conclusion: The proposed metasurface offers a promising route for comprehensive EM protection in RF front-end systems.

title: How Large Should Academic Departments Be?
authors: Jan Bachmann, Lisette Esp\'in-Noboa, Fariba Karimi, Daniel B. Larremore, Gerardo I\~niguez, Aaron Clauset
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Academic departments are the primary unit of scholarship and education at universities, and they vary vastly in their sizes. However, the consequences and natural dynamics of department size are poorly understood. Small departments face disproportionate teaching and administrative overhead per faculty member, while large ones face coordination costs and thematic incoherence. Here, we characterize and model the dynamics of academic department sizes using [MATH] U.S.-based departments in eight academic domains. Across all domains, similar broad-tailed distributions reveal a common size range from 4 to 23 faculty members, widening across domains at its upper border. Annual size-dependent closure risks and growth rates indicate that stability is greatest in this size range: below it, small departments either close or grow quickly; within it, closure risk is low and sizes stabilize; above it, large departments can persist, with marginal attrition and minimal closure risk. An analytically tractable model of size-dependent coagulation and fragmentation, informed only by the aggregated size distribution, reproduces department dynamics across the full size range. Rescaling each domain by its most stable size reveals a common regression toward the stable range across most domains. Our results establish academic departments as organizations with natural size dynamics defined by a grow-or-close pattern for the smallest departments, and a weak pressure against unlimited growth for the largest.
tldr: This paper studies the size dynamics of academic departments using a coagulation-fragmentation model, finding a stable size range of 4-23 faculty members across domains.
motivation: Understanding the consequences and natural dynamics of department size is important for university organization, but small departments face high overhead while large ones suffer coordination costs.
method: The authors analyze historical data on U.S. academic departments across eight domains, fitting a size-dependent coagulation-fragmentation model to reproduce observed size distributions and dynamics.
result: Department sizes follow broad-tailed distributions with a common stable range of 4-23 faculty; below this range departments either close or grow quickly, within it stability is high, and above it large departments persist with minimal closure risk.
conclusion: Academic departments exhibit natural size dynamics with a grow-or-close pattern for small departments and weak pressure against unlimited growth for large ones, suggesting an optimal size range for stability.

title: Producing A Complete Nuclear Data Library For Adjoint Monte Carlo Simulations
authors: Paul Rovel (LTSD, ENPC), Coline Larmier (cea-Des), Davide Mancusi (LTSD, SERMA), Andrea Zoia
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radiation shielding applications related to reactor design typically involve situations where the source region (the core) is much larger than the detector region (a dosimeter). In such cases, the efficiency of Monte Carlo simulation might be significantly increased by solving the adjoint transport equation: adjoint particles are born from the detector, undergo adjoint ('reversed') flights and collisions, and accumulate their tallies in the source region. A key prerequisite to sample the adjoint collision events is the preparation of adjoint nuclear data. In this work, we propose a general method able to handle the diversity of nuclear reactions available in modern neutron data evaluations, and ultimately create a full adjoint nuclear data library. This is a stepping stone in view of implementing adjoint sampling schemes in TRIPOLI-5 __ , the next-generation Monte Carlo code developed by CEA and ASNR. We validate this strategy based on a relevant continuous energy benchmark configuration involving mixtures of heavy and light nuclides, and we compare our results to those obtained by standard forward Monte Carlo simulations.
tldr: This paper presents a method to generate a complete adjoint nuclear data library for Monte Carlo simulations in radiation shielding, with no connection to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Adjoint Monte Carlo simulations can significantly improve efficiency for radiation shielding problems where the source region is much larger than the detector, but require adjoint nuclear data that are not readily available.
method: The authors propose a general method to handle the diversity of nuclear reactions in modern neutron data evaluations and create a full adjoint nuclear data library, validated on a continuous energy benchmark.
result: The adjoint simulation results match those from standard forward Monte Carlo simulations, demonstrating the validity of the adjoint data library.
conclusion: This work provides a stepping stone for implementing adjoint sampling schemes in the TRIPOLI-5 Monte Carlo code, improving efficiency for reactor design shielding applications.

title: Lagrange Interpolation Processes Based On The Zeros Of anti-Gauss Jacobi Polynomials
authors: Patricia D\'iaz de Alba, Luisa Fermo, Valerio Loi, Donatella Occorsio
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces and investigates a new Lagrange interpolation process based on the zeros of anti-Gauss Jacobi polynomials. Fundamental properties of anti-Gauss nodes, including their asymptotic distribution, are established, together with estimates for the associated polynomials and their derivatives. These results provide the basis for the construction of an interpolation process whose weighted Lebesgue constants exhibit logarithmic growth, ensuring optimal approximation properties. Compared with previously known interpolation schemes based on Jacobi nodes, the proposed process achieves optimal Lebesgue constants for a shifted range of endpoint weight parameters, allowing the use of smaller endpoint weight exponents. Convergence estimates are established for functions in suitable weighted Sobolev spaces, and numerical experiments support the theoretical findings.
tldr: This paper studies Lagrange interpolation using zeros of anti-Gauss Jacobi polynomials, focusing on approximation theory and numerical analysis.
motivation: To develop an interpolation process with optimal Lebesgue constants for a wider range of weight parameters than traditional Jacobi nodes.
method: The authors analyze the asymptotic distribution of anti-Gauss nodes, derive estimates for associated polynomials and derivatives, and construct a Lagrange interpolation scheme.
result: The weighted Lebesgue constants exhibit logarithmic growth, ensuring optimal approximation; convergence estimates are proven in weighted Sobolev spaces and confirmed numerically.
conclusion: The proposed interpolation process achieves optimal approximation properties for a shifted range of endpoint weight parameters, improving upon existing Jacobi-based schemes.

title: Parametric Neural r-Adaptivity For Isogeometric Analysis Via Residual Minimization
authors: El\'ias Caru, David Pardo, Judit Mu\~noz-Matute
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose an r-adaptive neural algorithm for Isogeometric Analysis (IGA) based on residual minimization. The boundary-value problem is solved using a standard conforming Galerkin formulation, while a neural network relocates the interior knots. A strong-form residual in the sense of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) controls a norm stronger than the energy (H^1) error. We therefore weight it by classical a posteriori theory: element residuals scaled by the local mesh size, interface flux jumps, and Neumann boundary residuals yield a computable estimator of the energy error, which we minimize with respect to the knots. For coercive problems on admissible mesh families, this estimator is reliable and locally efficient up to oscillation terms; beyond that regime, the same loss remains well-defined and extends differentiable r-adaptivity to indefinite and advection-dominated problems. In the parametric setting, the network maps each parameter to a knot-density function in a single evaluation; since it outputs a density rather than a fixed-dimensional vector of knot locations, one trained network produces an admissible mesh at any refinement level. Mesh gradients are obtained by reverse-mode automatic differentiation through the discrete solution equation. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions illustrate that the method concentrates degrees of freedom near singularities, material interfaces, and boundary layers, improving accuracy for a fixed number of degrees of freedom.
tldr: This paper proposes a neural r-adaptive method for isogeometric analysis using residual minimization to relocate knots.
motivation: To improve accuracy in isogeometric analysis by adaptively relocating knots using neural networks and residual-based error estimators.
method: A neural network maps parameters to knot-density functions; the mesh is adapted by minimizing a strong-form residual weighted by classical a posteriori error indicators.
result: The method concentrates degrees of freedom near singularities, material interfaces, and boundary layers, improving accuracy for a fixed number of degrees of freedom.
conclusion: The proposed approach provides a differentiable r-adaptivity framework that extends to indefinite and advection-dominated problems.

title: Semiparametric Inference On Identification Sets In Choice Modeling
authors: Antoine Scheid, Jia Wan, Guy Aridor, Nathan Kallus, Aurelien Bibaut
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a discrete choice model, choice probabilities observed for a finite collection of choice sets may not identify a counterfactual choice probability under an unobserved choice set. We represent this counterfactual probability as a linear functional of a mixing distribution. Because the target is a functional of a distribution whose support is not restricted to a finite set, the parameter space is infinite-dimensional, while the data impose only finitely many moment restrictions. Therefore, observed choice probabilities need not point identify such a target. The identified set is defined as the set of target values compatible with observed choice probabilities. Rather than imposing conditions to ensure point identification, we characterize the identified set, and conduct inference on its lower and upper endpoints. We represent each endpoint as the value of a linear program over probability measures, and give conditions to obtain pathwise differentiability of the identification bounds. As a consequence, we are able to prove asymptotic normality of plug-in endpoint estimators. Finally, we provide an Expectation-Maximization-like algorithm for certifying membership of candidate values in the identified set and establish local convergence guarantees.
tldr: This paper develops semiparametric inference methods for identification sets in discrete choice models, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper addresses the problem of non-identification of counterfactual choice probabilities in discrete choice models, which is a statistical issue in econometrics.
method: The authors characterize the identified set as the value of a linear program over probability measures and derive asymptotic normality of plug-in estimators.
result: They provide conditions for pathwise differentiability of identification bounds and propose an EM-like algorithm for certifying membership in the identified set.
conclusion: The work contributes to semiparametric inference in choice modeling but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Safe Stabilizing Linear Feedback: Necessary And Sufficient Conditions, Optimality, And Margins
authors: Pol Mestres, Shima Sadat Mousavi, Pio Ong, Aaron D. Ames
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Control barrier functions (CBFs) have become an important controller design tool for autonomous systems subject to safety constraints. Despite their popularity, recent works have shown that CBF-based controllers can destabilize the internal dynamics of the system. In this paper, we consider linear systems with affine safety constraints and design linear feedback controllers that satisfy high-order CBF (HOCBF) constraints while rendering the origin globally exponentially stable. We first characterize the exact class of all linear gain matrices that globally satisfy the HOCBF constraints, including necessary and sufficient conditions for when this class is nonempty. Then, by leveraging the recently introduced notion of CBF output dynamics and CBF internal dynamics, we provide the necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of stabilizing gain matrices within that class. Finally, we show that Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) and robust control problems can be solved while being constrained within this class of safe and stabilizing gain matrices, through standard linear control techniques such as algebraic Riccati equations (AREs) and Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs). We illustrate our results in a simulation example.
tldr: This paper presents necessary and sufficient conditions for designing linear feedback controllers that satisfy high-order control barrier function constraints while ensuring global exponential stability.
motivation: Control barrier functions are popular for safety-critical control, but can destabilize internal dynamics; the authors aim to design safe yet stabilizing linear controllers.
method: The authors characterize the class of linear gain matrices satisfying HOCBF constraints, derive conditions for existence of stabilizing gains, and incorporate LQR and robust control via AREs and LMIs.
result: Necessary and sufficient conditions for safe stabilizing linear feedback are provided, and optimal control problems are solved within the constrained gain class.
conclusion: The work bridges safety and stability in linear systems, enabling optimal control with safety guarantees.

title: The Two Momenta Of An Elastic Rod: A Hamiltonian Picture On Framed Lie Groups
authors: Thomas Lessinnes
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The equilibrium equations of elastic rods can be obtained by balancing forces and moments, or by rendering a potential energy stationary. For complex filaments the energy route asks less of one's mechanical intuition. However, in the classical Hamiltonian picture, the components of the generalized momenta are postulated a priori and their physical meaning changes at the whim of the coordinate chart. Here, we draw on two ideas from mathematical physics. First, the extended tangent bundle of the configuration Lie group is framed by left-invariant vector fields. Second, we follow a one-dimensional reading of the Cartan--Lepage--Krupka theory of variational forms: in this setting the momenta are not postulated but forced. The Legendre transform becomes a linear change of frame, and a Poisson structure on the extended tangent bundle follows. For an isolated Cosserat rod, the momenta coincide, in every encoding of the rotation group, with the material force and moment familiar from rod theories. In the presence of interactions, two cases arise: interactions that depend only on the configuration, such as gravity, leave this identification intact; interactions that depend on the strains destroy it --- the conjugate momenta and the internal stresses part company. Because energies add, the momenta decompose into the internal stresses and an interaction contribution. Expressing the two factors of the Poisson bivector in different frames --- one adapted to the internal stresses, the other to the conjugate momenta --- then exposes the Hamiltonian flow directly in the internal variables. Applied to a tendon-actuated rod, where the standard passage to the Hamiltonian picture demands a nonlinear inversion, the construction delivers explicit equilibrium equations, the required inversion collapsing to a rank-one correction.
tldr: This paper develops a Hamiltonian formulation for elastic rods using framed Lie groups and variational forms, focusing on the physical interpretation of momenta.
motivation: To provide a geometrically rigorous Hamiltonian description of elastic rods where momenta are derived from variational principles rather than postulated, clarifying their physical meaning.
method: Uses left-invariant framing of the extended tangent bundle of the configuration Lie group and applies Cartan-Lepage-Krupka theory of variational forms to derive momenta and Poisson structure.
result: For an isolated Cosserat rod, momenta coincide with material force and moment; for interacting rods, momenta decompose into internal stresses and interaction contributions, simplifying the Hamiltonian flow.
conclusion: The construction yields explicit equilibrium equations for tendon-actuated rods, reducing a nonlinear inversion to a rank-one correction.

title: On Convergence Of Solutions To Nonlocal Optimal Control Problems With Quasi-minimization Constraints
authors: Joshua M. Siktar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies a new class of nonlocal optimal control problems where the constraints involve approximations of minimizers of quasiconvex energies. These problems are parameterized by a fractional parameter [MATH] and a horizon parameter [MATH], and the energy density depends on a nonlocal fractional gradient. Here, the constraint consists of finding quasi-minimizers with respect to the quasiconvex energy. Despite the fact that the energies of interest may not have unique minimizers, we may prove the existence of solutions to this class of control problems. The constraint in Cueto-Siktar 2026 was finding global minimizers of the energy, and this problem's main limitation was an inability to prove convergence of solutions for the nonlocal control problems to those of a corresponding local, PDE-constrained optimal control problem. While this issue arises from the lack of uniqueness of minimizers for the constraining energy, we get stronger convergence results with our new choice of constraints. Namely, we obtain convergence of minimizers for nonlocal optimal control problems that have a general cost functional depending on the nonlocal gradient.
tldr: This paper studies nonlocal optimal control problems with quasi-minimization constraints, focusing on convergence of solutions to local PDE-constrained problems.
motivation: Previous work could not prove convergence due to non-uniqueness of minimizers; this paper uses quasi-minimizers to achieve stronger convergence results.
method: The authors formulate control problems with constraints involving approximations of minimizers of quasiconvex energies, parameterized by fractional and horizon parameters, and analyze convergence as the nonlocal parameter vanishes.
result: They prove existence of solutions and obtain convergence of minimizers for general cost functionals depending on the nonlocal gradient.
conclusion: The quasi-minimization approach overcomes limitations of global minimizer constraints, enabling convergence to local optimal control problems.

authors: Austin Anderson, Mirjana Jovovic, Wayne Smith

title: Stackelberg Games With A Robust Leader
authors: Juan Li, Jianfeng Zhang, Zimu Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study a Stackelberg game with one leader and multiple followers. Given the leader's control, the followers solve a Nash game with possibly multiple equilibria. We consider a robust leader who considers the worst scenario, namely the followers would select the equilibrium worst for the leader. By using the weak formulation, the problem induces a zero sum game problem with open loop controls, which is time inconsistent. We shall characterize the last problem through an HJB equation on the Wasserstein space of probability measures. The principal-agent problem with one principal and multiple agents can be viewed as a special case of our problem, but with certain constraints.
tldr: This paper studies a Stackelberg game with a robust leader and multiple followers, using weak formulation and HJB equations on Wasserstein space.
motivation: The authors aim to model a leader who considers the worst-case equilibrium selection by followers in a Stackelberg game with multiple Nash equilibria.
method: They formulate the problem as a zero-sum game with open-loop controls, addressing time inconsistency via an HJB equation on the Wasserstein space of probability measures.
result: The problem is characterized through the HJB equation, and the principal-agent problem is shown as a special case with constraints.
conclusion: The framework provides a rigorous approach to robust decision-making in hierarchical games with multiple followers.

title: Singular Suspension Flows And Infinite Topological Entropy
authors: Sergio Roma\~na Jonatas Marinho S. Araujo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a dense set of homeomorphisms with infinite topological entropy whose associated pseudo-singular suspension flows have finite entropy -- and indeed, arbitrarily small positive values can be achieved -- showing that infinite entropy is not preserved under singular time changes. Complementing this, we prove that for a residual set of homeomorphisms, all pseudo-singular suspensions retain positive entropy. We also prove that for any [MATH], there exists a compact n-dimensional manifold admitting a minimal homeomorphism with infinite topological entropy; for such minimal homeomorphisms, a suitably chosen pseudo-singular suspension with a single singularity has zero entropy. Our results reveal that while positivity of entropy is generically stable, its infinitude is fragile under singular reparametrizations.
tldr: This paper studies topological entropy of singular suspension flows and homeomorphisms, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how infinite topological entropy behaves under singular time changes in dynamical systems.
method: They construct dense sets of homeomorphisms with infinite entropy and analyze their pseudo-singular suspension flows, using techniques from dynamical systems theory.
result: They show that infinite entropy is not preserved under singular time changes, but positivity of entropy is generically stable.
conclusion: The fragility of infinite entropy under singular reparametrizations is demonstrated, with examples on compact manifolds.

title: Strategic Inference Of Adversarial Navigation Objectives For Unmanned Underwater Vehicles
authors: Xu Yang Ruimeng Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study destination inference for adversarial unmanned underwater navigation in a spatially varying current field. The red vehicle is modeled as approximately following a Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) time-optimal path toward an unknown destination, while a blue vehicle observes a noisy realization of that trajectory. We derive a continuous-time likelihood model for this problem and obtain a closed-form local maximum likelihood estimator, a constant-memory multi-period estimator, and an asymptotic Cram\'er-Rao efficiency result. The Fisher information is governed by a combined score kernel with two additive components, a policy-mean sensitivity and a reference-path sensitivity, and a multiplicative drift sensitivity whose leading geometric contribution is a contraction of the current Hessian with the Jacobi field of the HJ characteristic flow. All three sensitivities are induced by that Jacobi field, yielding a computable link between current-field geometry and destination identifiability. We further extend the framework to a sweep-dependent observation model and formulate an active sweep-design problem for the blue team. Numerical experiments in vortex and channel-shear currents validate the Cram\'er-Rao prediction and illustrate how current geometry determines which destinations can be reliably inferred.
tldr: This paper studies destination inference for adversarial underwater navigation using Hamilton-Jacobi theory and Cramér-Rao bounds, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To infer the destination of an adversarial unmanned underwater vehicle from noisy trajectory observations in a spatially varying current field.
method: Derives a continuous-time likelihood model, closed-form local MLE, constant-memory multi-period estimator, and asymptotic Cramér-Rao efficiency; analyzes Fisher information via a combined score kernel with policy-mean, reference-path, and drift sensitivities induced by the Jacobi field of the HJ characteristic flow.
result: The Fisher information is governed by a combined score kernel with three sensitivities, all induced by the Jacobi field, providing a computable link between current-field geometry and destination identifiability.
conclusion: Current geometry determines which destinations can be reliably inferred, validated by numerical experiments in vortex and channel-shear currents.

title: Exponential Convergence Can Happen In Weighted Birkhoff Averages Via Quasi-periodicity With Arbitrary Nonresonance And Low Regularity
authors: Zhicheng Tong
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since Krengel's work [Kre78] in 1978, it has been widely known that no effective rate of convergence exists in the ergodic theorem. For toral translations, however, by choosing appropriate weights one can accelerate the convergence of ergodic averages to an exponential rate, but this intuitively requires both highly nonresonant frequencies and very regular observables. In this paper, we uncover a new phenomenon: even for any given nonresonant frequency, there exists a non-trivial family of weights and observables of low regularity such that the weighted Birkhoff averages along quasi-periodic orbits converge at a quantitative, uniform, and exponential rate. This not only yields a finer understanding of the deep interaction between nonresonance and regularity in ergodic theory, but also stands as a weighted counterpart to a Yoccoz-type result [Yoc80,Yoc95].
tldr: This paper studies exponential convergence of weighted Birkhoff averages for quasi-periodic orbits with low regularity observables, a result in ergodic theory.
motivation: To understand the interplay between nonresonance and regularity in ergodic averages, and to extend known results on exponential convergence to broader conditions.
method: The author constructs a family of weights and observables with low regularity and proves that weighted Birkhoff averages converge exponentially for any given nonresonant frequency.
result: Exponential convergence is achieved even for low-regularity observables, contrary to previous belief that high regularity was required.
conclusion: The work provides a weighted counterpart to Yoccoz-type results and deepens the understanding of convergence rates in ergodic theory.

authors: Amir Algom, Snir Ben Ovadia, Federico Rodriguez Hertz, Mario Shannon

First, we construct a [MATH] iterated function system which is not [MATH]-conjugate to self-similar, but which nevertheless admits a stationary measure that is not Rajchman. Second, for every strongly separated Bernoulli convolution [MATH] and every [MATH], we construct a [MATH]-diffeomorphism [MATH] such that [MATH] is constant on [MATH], yet the image measure [MATH] has polynomial Fourier decay. All constructions are within the framework of pseudo-affine iterated function systems, previously introduced by the authors.

title: Piml-ofem: A New Large-Scale Structural Analysis Method Based On Problem-Independent Machine Learning And Overlapping Finite Element Technique
authors: Yilin Guo, Chang Liu, Zongliang Du, Jin Liu, Jingyu Feng, Xinyang Zhang, Yang Li, Tianxing Yang, Changyu Shen, Xu Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-resolution analysis and design of large-scale heterogeneous structures require accurate reduced-order models and efficient online computation. Existing multiscale methods must repeatedly construct local basis functions for different material distributions, whereas substructure-based problem-independent machine learning (PIML) methods can be limited by prescribed boundary displacement interpolation. We propose PIML-OFEM, an overlapping finite element method accelerated by problem-independent machine learning. Each substructure retains only its corner-node degrees of freedom. Oversampled numerical basis functions are constructed by solving local elasticity problems on extended domains and restricting the solutions to the target substructure, eliminating prescribed displacement interpolation on its boundary. Independently constructed local bases are blended through a partition-of-unity overlapping formulation to obtain a globally continuous displacement field. A U-Net learns the mapping from local Young's modulus distributions to numerical basis functions, replacing repeated online local solves and allowing the model to be reused across load cases and global boundary conditions. Numerical examples show close agreement with fine-scale finite element results in displacement and elemental strain energy. PIML-OFEM reduces online computational cost relative to direct finite element analysis and improves accuracy over PIML substructure models based on linear boundary interpolation. In topology optimization, the method supports stable high-resolution iterations with small filter radii and preserves fine-scale features, including local patterns resembling rank-2 microstructures. The framework provides an efficient physics-data approach for large-scale heterogeneous structural analysis and high-resolution topology optimization.
tldr: This paper proposes a machine learning-accelerated overlapping finite element method for large-scale structural analysis and topology optimization.
motivation: Existing multiscale methods require repeated construction of local basis functions for different material distributions, and substructure-based PIML methods are limited by prescribed boundary displacement interpolation.
method: The method uses oversampled numerical basis functions constructed on extended domains, blended via partition-of-unity overlapping formulation, with a U-Net learning the mapping from Young's modulus distributions to basis functions.
result: Numerical examples show close agreement with fine-scale FEM in displacement and strain energy, with reduced online cost and improved accuracy over linear boundary interpolation.
conclusion: The framework provides an efficient physics-data approach for large-scale heterogeneous structural analysis and high-resolution topology optimization.

title: Learning From Downstream Prices: Robust Upstream Decisions With Revealed Pricing Optimality
authors: Zhiqiang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Problem definition. An upstream firm often observes the retail prices and sales generated by a better-informed downstream partner, but not the consumer valuation distribution that drives those decisions. Conventional demand analysis treats a retail price as a covariate. We study how the upstream firm can instead exploit the fact that the observed price was chosen optimally, particularly when the transaction history is sparse. Methodology/results. Under regular consumer valuations, a downstream retailer's optimal price reveals a virtual-value condition in addition to the demand quantile observed at that price. We use these signals to construct a shape-constrained ambiguity set whose feasible local family is a scalar interval. We show that the worst-case local model is attained at an endpoint, reducing a continuous distributional problem to a two-scenario robust newsvendor. We also characterize how revealed optimality tightens a quantile-only benchmark and how bounded decision errors erode this advantage. Across six regular valuation models, three (five) historical records raise the mean oracle-profit ratio from 0.892 to 0.955 (0.918 to 0.986); the endpoint method matches a 1,001-point ambiguity grid and is more than 700 times faster. Managerial implications. Downstream prices should be treated as strategic decision data rather than merely as demand covariates. The proposed framework allows an upstream firm to convert a small number of pricing records into a tractable decision rule, while providing a principled fallback to quantile-only information when downstream decisions are unreliable.
tldr: This paper studies how an upstream firm can exploit the optimality of downstream retail prices to improve decision-making under sparse data.
motivation: Upstream firms often lack direct knowledge of consumer valuations but observe downstream prices that are set optimally; conventional demand analysis treats prices as covariates, ignoring the strategic information they contain.
method: The paper uses revealed pricing optimality to derive virtual-value conditions, constructs a shape-constrained ambiguity set, and reduces the distributional problem to a two-scenario robust newsvendor model.
result: With three (five) historical records, the mean oracle-profit ratio improves from 0.892 to 0.955 (0.918 to 0.986); the endpoint method matches a 1,001-point grid and is 700 times faster.
conclusion: Downstream prices should be treated as strategic decision data; the framework provides tractable decision rules from few records and a fallback to quantile-only information when decisions are unreliable.

title: A Physics-informed Neural Network For Improving Surface Reconstruction Of Intracranial Saccular Aneurysms Via Variational Membrane Equilibrium
authors: Hyomin Ryu, Seung Hwan Kim, Jaemin Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intracranial saccular aneurysms (ISAs) pose severe health risks, yet conventional population-based risk stratification scores (PHASES, UIATS, and ELAPSS) offer limited capacity for patient-specific rupture risk assessment. Image-based computational approaches have gained prominence, but traditional surface reconstruction relies on mathematical smoothing (e.g., L-curve criteria) that indiscriminately suppresses both imaging artifacts and genuine pathological features such as rupture-prone blebs. Although Laplace's membrane equilibrium ([MATH]) has long governed aneurysm wall mechanics (Humphrey and Kyriacou [Neurol. Res., 18 (1996)]), its integration into geometric reconstruction pipelines remains unexplored. This work introduces a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework with B-spline representations, whose key contributions are: (i) embedding the variational equilibrium condition ([MATH]) as a physics-informed loss that replaces the mathematical L-curve criterion with a biomechanically grounded artifact discrimination, (ii) developing a Manifold-Consistent CNN ansatz that preserves the closed-surface topology of vascular geometries, and (iii) establishing a Laplace equilibrium-driven reconstruction that filters imaging noise while preserving diagnostically critical high-curvature features. Application to patient-specific clinical datasets demonstrates that the framework eliminates non-physical concave artifacts without compromising genuine geometric anomalies. Clinical evaluation by a practicing neurosurgeon confirms that the resulting risk map---with rupture risk concentrated at the dome apex---is consistent with intraoperative observations, establishing a computational biomarker foundation for patient-specific rupture risk assessment of intracranial saccular aneurysms.
tldr: This paper uses a physics-informed neural network to improve surface reconstruction of intracranial aneurysms by embedding Laplace's membrane equilibrium.
motivation: Conventional surface reconstruction methods indiscriminately suppress both imaging artifacts and genuine pathological features, limiting patient-specific rupture risk assessment.
method: A PINN with B-spline representations and a Manifold-Consistent CNN ansatz is trained with a physics-informed loss based on variational membrane equilibrium to filter noise while preserving high-curvature features.
result: The framework eliminates non-physical concave artifacts and produces risk maps consistent with intraoperative observations.
conclusion: The approach establishes a computational biomarker foundation for patient-specific rupture risk assessment of intracranial saccular aneurysms.

title: Distortion In The Group Of Locally Monotone Homeomorphisms Of A Cantor Set And In The Group Of Generalized Interval Exchange Transformations
authors: Nancy Guelman (UDELAR, IMERL), Emmanuel Militon
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let f be either a generalized interval exchange transformation or a locally monotone homeomorphism of a Cantor subset of the real line. In this article, we prove that the following are equivalent. 1. The number of discontinuities of f^n is bounded. 2. There exists n [MATH] 1 such that the element f is conjugate to the restriction to a closed invariant subset of a disjoint union of n circles of a homeomorphism of this disjoint union of circles. 3. The element f is distorted in the group of generalized interval exchange transformations or in the group of locally monotone homeomorphisms of the Cantor subset.
tldr: This paper studies distortion in groups of locally monotone homeomorphisms of a Cantor set and generalized interval exchange transformations, proving equivalence between bounded discontinuities, conjugacy to a circle homeomorphism, and distortion.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize distorted elements in these specific groups, which is a problem in geometric group theory and dynamical systems.
method: The paper uses combinatorial and dynamical arguments to analyze the growth of discontinuities under iteration and to construct conjugacies.
result: The three conditions (bounded number of discontinuities of iterates, conjugacy to a circle homeomorphism, and distortion in the group) are equivalent.
conclusion: This provides a complete characterization of distorted elements in these groups, contributing to the understanding of group structure and dynamics.

title: Designing Eco-Efficient Biowaste Valorisation Systems: Effects Of Transport Distance And Facility Scale
authors: Christian Ottini (sayfood), Gwenola Yannou-Le Bris (sayfood), Sandra Domenek (sayfood), Felipe Buendia
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing deployment of separate biowaste collection across Europe raises questions regarding environmentally and economically optimal treatment strategies. From this perspective, the balance between decentralised and centralised infrastructure is a potential lever to consider. The choice of technologies is another. Composting and anaerobic digestion (AD) offer viable circular bioeconomy pathways, but their performance depends on transport distance, facility size, seasonal waste fluctuations, and technological efficiency. Threshold distances and scale-dependent interactions affecting the environmental and economic performance of treatment plants remain poorly characterised. This study develops a unified techno-economic and life cycle assessment framework to quantify how transport constraints and treatment capacities shape biowaste valorisation systems. Three facility scales for composting and AD are evaluated across a range of transport distances and compared with local incineration in terms of environmental and economic performance. Transport burdens are modelled using vehicle life cycle assessment (LCA) and realistic heavy-duty truck data for electric-, gas-, and diesel-powered vehicles. Results reveal non-linear trade-offs between scale and transport, with zero-distance composting yielding the lowest combined impacts. Across all scenarios, 45 configurations outperform local incineration economically and environmentally, while 111 remain environmentally preferable despite higher costs, thus providing quantitative guidance for infrastructure planning.
tldr: This paper develops a techno-economic and life cycle assessment framework for biowaste valorisation systems, comparing composting and anaerobic digestion across different transport distances and facility scales.
motivation: The increasing deployment of separate biowaste collection in Europe requires environmentally and economically optimal treatment strategies, but threshold distances and scale-dependent interactions are poorly characterized.
method: A unified techno-economic and life cycle assessment framework is developed, evaluating three facility scales for composting and anaerobic digestion across a range of transport distances, using vehicle LCA with electric-, gas-, and diesel-powered truck data.
result: Zero-distance composting yields the lowest combined impacts; 45 configurations outperform local incineration economically and environmentally, while 111 are environmentally preferable despite higher costs.
conclusion: The study provides quantitative guidance for infrastructure planning, highlighting non-linear trade-offs between scale and transport.

title: Non-Negative Conjugate Gradients
authors: Martin Stoll Thomas Schmelzer
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The conjugate gradient method (CG) solves a symmetric positive definite (SPD) system [MATH], but does not respect [MATH]. We develop non-negative conjugate gradients, a solver for the bound-constrained quadratic [MATH] subject to [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], with [MATH] present only in the equality-augmented variant. The solver wraps CG in a primal-dual active-set loop: each step solves the unconstrained system over the free variables, drops variables that turn negative, re-admits any bound variable with negative reduced gradient, and restarts CG. These toggles are the principal pivots of the linear complementarity problem [MATH], well defined since [MATH] is a [MATH]-matrix. motivation: The conjugate gradient method does not respect non-negativity constraints, which are common in many applications. The authors aim to extend CG to handle such constraints efficiently.
method: The method wraps CG in a primal-dual active-set loop that solves unconstrained systems over free variables, drops negative variables, and re-admits bound variables with negative reduced gradient, using principal pivots and a Bland fallback for termination.
result: The algorithm converges in finitely many outer steps, matches the exact solver's sign decisions under inexact inner solves, and on dense synthetic problems outperforms Lawson-Hanson and interior-point solvers by an order of magnitude.
conclusion: The non-negative conjugate gradient method provides an efficient, matrix-free solver for bound-constrained quadratic programs with M-matrices, with guaranteed finite termination.

title: High-order Finite Element Method For Perfect Conductivity And Linear Elasticity With Nearly Touching Inclusions
authors: Buyang Li, Haigang Li, Yonglin Li, Peihao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In perfect conductivity and linear elasticity problems, the electric field and stress always become highly concentrated within narrow regions between adjacent perfect (rigid) inclusions, and blow up as the distance between inclusions approaches zero. The design of high-order numerical methods with rigorous error analysis for such concentration problems remains open. In this paper, we present the first high-order finite element method for solving these problems. Our approach is based on asymptotic estimates of high-order derivatives of solutions, employing a graded mesh and auxiliary basis functions specifically designed from these derivative estimates. We prove that the proposed method converges with an [MATH]-error bound of [MATH] and the error bound is independent of the distance (possibly approaching zero) between inclusions, where [MATH] is the mesh size and [MATH] is the degree of finite elements. Numerical examples in both two and three dimensions are presented to demonstrate the convergence rates of the numerical solutions. In particular, the blow-up behaviors of the gradients of solutions are demonstrated when the inclusions approach each other.
tldr: This paper develops a high-order finite element method for perfect conductivity and linear elasticity problems with nearly touching inclusions.
motivation: The electric field and stress become highly concentrated between adjacent inclusions, and designing high-order numerical methods with rigorous error analysis for such problems has been an open challenge.
method: The method uses asymptotic estimates of high-order derivatives to design a graded mesh and auxiliary basis functions, and proves convergence with error bound independent of inclusion distance.
result: The proposed method achieves an error bound of O(h^{k+1}) where h is mesh size and k is polynomial degree, independent of the distance between inclusions, demonstrated in 2D and 3D examples.
conclusion: This is the first high-order finite element method for these concentration problems, with rigorous error analysis and numerical validation.

title: Analysis And Structure-preserving Discretization Of The Heat-GLM System
authors: Firas Dhaouadi (bordeaux INP, IMB, UB, CARDAMOM), Laura R{\'i}o-Mart{\'i}n (CARDAMOM, IMB, UB), Michael Dumbser
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a prototype hyperbolic system arising from the coupling of Generalized-Lagrangian-Multiplier (GLM) curl-cleaning with linear acoustics. We first show that, in the absence of dissipation, the equations can be rigorously derived from an underlying variational principle and that the resulting system is symmetric-hyperbolic. Further analysis shows that it not only conserves the total energy but also admits a set of invariants consisting of quadratic combinations of differential operators applied to the state variables. The addition of a stiff relaxation source term allows the system to be extended to dissipative dynamics, describing, for example, Cattaneo-type heat transfer processes that are asymptotically compatible with the Fourier law in the stiff relaxation limit; in this case, the total energy and invariants are dissipated accordingly. A new semi-implicit compatible numerical scheme on staggered grids is developed to solve this system while exactly preserving its key properties at the discrete level. In particular, we prove that the scheme is asymptotic-preserving in the Fourier limit, with a convergence rate depending on the initial data. We also show that the scheme conserves exactly the total energy as well as all the invariants in the absence of relaxation, and dissipates them consistently in its presence. These findings are demonstrated on a set of representative test cases.
tldr: This paper studies a hyperbolic system for heat transfer with GLM curl-cleaning, focusing on structure-preserving discretization.
motivation: To develop a numerical scheme that exactly preserves key properties like energy and invariants for a hyperbolic heat conduction model.
method: The authors derive the system from a variational principle, analyze its invariants, and propose a semi-implicit staggered-grid scheme that is asymptotic-preserving.
result: The scheme conserves total energy and invariants without relaxation, and dissipates them consistently with relaxation; convergence is demonstrated on test cases.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a structure-preserving discretization for the heat-GLM system, ensuring physical consistency at the discrete level.

title: Nonparametric Inference For Semigroup Blocks Of Switching Diffusions
authors: Yuzhong Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Regime-conditioned transition probabilities and moments are basic inputs for prediction and decision making in hybrid systems, but their short-time infinitesimal structure is not directly observable. We study nonparametric estimation of regime-indexed semigroup blocks for switching diffusions observed together with their regimes. A Dynkin--Taylor expansion identifies the first two block-generator coefficients, and localized probes recover switching intensities, drift, and diffusion. Under shrinking meshes, a common-design difference cancels the localized level and yields a martingale array; nonoverlapping second differences preserve within-block covariance and produce the variance factor two. The resulting first- and second-order estimators are asymptotically normal, admit feasible studentization, and support short-horizon approximation and specification checks for interactions among primitive coefficients. Fixed-mesh local-polynomial theory and a numerical study complement the recovery results.
tldr: This paper studies nonparametric estimation of regime-conditioned semigroup blocks for switching diffusions, a topic in stochastic processes and statistics.
motivation: Regime-conditioned transition probabilities are crucial for prediction in hybrid systems, but their short-time infinitesimal structure is not directly observable.
method: A Dynkin-Taylor expansion identifies block-generator coefficients, and localized probes recover switching intensities, drift, and diffusion using martingale arrays and nonoverlapping second differences.
result: First- and second-order estimators are asymptotically normal, admit feasible studentization, and support short-horizon approximation and specification checks.
conclusion: The proposed nonparametric method effectively recovers infinitesimal parameters of switching diffusions, validated by theory and numerical study.

title: Finite-Time Stabilization Of Linear Systems Via Optimal Control
authors: Weihao Weng (L2S), Yacine Chitour (L2S), Paolo Mason
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an optimal control framework for achieving finite-time stabilization of linear systems. By introducing a suitably constructed integral cost function, we derive a new class of nonlinear controllers that guarantee finite-time stability through the application of the optimality principle. The relationship between the resulting optimal control law and the associated value function is analyzed, leading to the derivation of a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation and the study of its regularity properties. Numerical simulations validate the theoretical findings and illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Furthermore, a discussion on estimating the convergence time is provided.
tldr: This paper presents an optimal control framework for finite-time stabilization of linear systems, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to achieve finite-time stabilization of linear systems using optimal control, which is a classical control theory problem.
method: The authors introduce an integral cost function and derive nonlinear controllers via the optimality principle, analyzing the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation.
result: Numerical simulations validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for finite-time stabilization.
conclusion: The proposed optimal control framework successfully guarantees finite-time stability for linear systems, with a discussion on convergence time estimation.

title: Accelerating The Canonical Polyadic Alternating Least Squares Optimization Via A Randomized Interpolative Decomposition
authors: Israa Fakih, Laura Grigori, Karl Pierce
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22194v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a novel leverage score-based sampling strategy for the randomized alternating least squares optimization (ALS) of the canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD-ALS). Unlike previous strategies, we determine row-wise samples for the CPD-ALS problem from the leverage scores of the target tensor which is being decomposed. We demonstrate that, when rows are sampled according to the leverage score distribution of the matricized target tensor, each least squares subproblem of the CPD-ALS problem achieves [MATH]relative accuracy in the residual norm with probability at least [MATH] using a sampling [MATH], where [MATH] is a constant, [MATH] is leverage score's approximation constant, [MATH] is the target rank and [MATH] captures the coherence between the Khatri Rao product (KRP) of the CPD factor matrices and the exact KRP; [MATH] decreases as the ALS iterates converge. To efficiently approximate the leverage score distribution for each matricization of the target tensor without explicitly computing leverage scores we use a randomized strong rank-revealing QR (sRRQR) factorizations, SE-QRCS. By construction, this QR-based leverage score sampling method outperforms previously published schemes as it does not, in principle, require the resampling of the target tensor or recomputing the leverage scores of the KRP, minimizing the computational and storage overhead of the CPD-ALS procedure.
tldr: This paper presents a randomized leverage score-based sampling strategy to accelerate the canonical polyadic alternating least squares optimization for tensor decomposition.
motivation: The canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD) via alternating least squares (ALS) is computationally expensive for large tensors; existing sampling methods for ALS subproblems are inefficient.
method: The authors propose sampling rows for each ALS subproblem based on leverage scores of the target tensor, approximated via a randomized strong rank-revealing QR factorization (SE-QRCS), avoiding explicit computation of leverage scores.
result: They prove that with high probability, each least squares subproblem achieves relative accuracy in the residual norm using a sample size that depends on the target rank and coherence, and the required sample size decreases as ALS converges.
conclusion: The proposed method reduces computational and storage overhead compared to previous schemes, making CPD-ALS more efficient for large-scale tensor decomposition.

title: Shape Optimisation For Adaptive $r$-refinement: The One-dimensional Case With Residual Based Error Estimators
authors: Philip J. Herbert
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider [MATH]-refinement for the finite element discretisation of a Poisson problem. The goal of [MATH]-refinement is to reposition the nodes of a computational mesh in order to better approximate the finite element error. Since the mesh is being moved, it naturally becomes linked to shape optimisation methods. We propose a standard optimisation algorithm for this [MATH]-refinement procedure and show that if one seeks to minimise the actual error - which one cannot generally calculate - one has an algorithm which will terminate. The most novel aspect of this work is to apply shape optimisation techniques to the a standard residual error estimator, which is a functional that is differentiable with respect to the mesh, when considered for the Poisson equation in one dimension. To illustrate the approach, a number of numerical experiments are presented, which verify the efficacy of the method.
tldr: This paper applies shape optimisation to adaptive r-refinement for finite element discretisation of a Poisson problem, using residual-based error estimators.
motivation: The goal is to improve finite element accuracy by repositioning mesh nodes, linking mesh movement to shape optimisation.
method: A standard optimisation algorithm minimises a residual error estimator that is differentiable with respect to the mesh in one dimension.
result: Numerical experiments verify the efficacy of the method for the Poisson equation in one dimension.
conclusion: The proposed shape optimisation approach for r-refinement is effective, but the work is purely numerical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Uniformly Quasiregular Maps Of $\mathbb{R}^n$ With Cantor Julia Sets
authors: Daniel A. Nicks
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any [MATH], we construct uniformly quasiregular self-maps of [MATH] of polynomial type for which the Julia set is a Cantor set.
tldr: This paper constructs uniformly quasiregular self-maps of R^n with Cantor Julia sets, a result in complex dynamics and quasiconformal geometry.
motivation: The study of uniformly quasiregular maps extends complex dynamics to higher dimensions, and constructing examples with Cantor Julia sets is a fundamental problem.
method: The author uses a construction based on expanding maps and conformal iterated function systems to build uniformly quasiregular maps of polynomial type.
result: For any n≥2, there exist uniformly quasiregular self-maps of R^n whose Julia set is a Cantor set.
conclusion: This provides new examples of uniformly quasiregular maps with fractal Julia sets, contributing to higher-dimensional complex dynamics.

title: On The Bollob\'as Theorem For Complex $C(K)$-spaces
authors: Helena Del R\'io Sheldon Dantas
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] and [MATH] be compact Hausdorff spaces. We prove a Bollob\'as-type theorem for operators between complex spaces of continuous functions. More precisely, every operator that almost attains its norm at an initial function can be approximated by a norm-attaining operator whose norm-attaining function remains close to the original one. Our proof combines the iterative method developed previously in the real case with the recent construction for complex measures. In particular, our result provides a quantitative strengthening of the complex version of the Johnson-Wolfe density theorem. As a byproduct of our construction, the same conclusion can be obtained when considering only compact operators.
tldr: This paper proves a Bollobás-type theorem for operators between complex spaces of continuous functions, extending a known result from real to complex case.
motivation: The Bollobás theorem is a classical result in functional analysis; extending it to complex C(K)-spaces fills a gap in the literature and provides a quantitative strengthening of the Johnson-Wolfe density theorem.
method: The proof combines an iterative method previously developed for the real case with a recent construction for complex measures.
result: Every operator that almost attains its norm at an initial function can be approximated by a norm-attaining operator whose norm-attaining function remains close to the original one; the same holds for compact operators.
conclusion: The result provides a quantitative version of the complex Johnson-Wolfe density theorem and advances the theory of norm-attaining operators in complex Banach spaces.

title: A Necessary Condition For The Existence Of Solutions Of Singular Linear-quadratic Vector Equations
authors: Axel Flinth Rishikesh Yadav
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the existence of solutions for systems of linear-quadratic vector equations with singular linear parts. We derive a sufficient condition for small right hand sides.
tldr: The paper studies existence conditions for solutions of singular linear-quadratic vector equations, which is a mathematical problem unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to derive necessary conditions for the existence of solutions to systems of linear-quadratic vector equations with singular linear parts, a purely mathematical problem.
method: The paper presents a sufficient condition for small right-hand sides, likely using linear algebra and fixed-point arguments.
result: A sufficient condition for the existence of solutions is derived, but no necessary condition is provided.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of linear-quadratic equations but has no connection to the user's research interests.

title: Explicit Iteration Complexity Of Exact Data-Driven Inverse Optimization For Integer Linear Programs
authors: Akira Kitaoka
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A data-driven inverse optimization problem (DDIOP) is the problem of estimating the objective-function parameters (weights) that explain observed optimal-solution data, and it arises in many applications, including integer linear programming (ILP). It is known that, by applying gradient-based optimization methods to the suboptimality loss, the inverse optimization of ILPs can be solved exactly within finitely many oracle iterations, and that the required number of iterations is bounded as [MATH] in terms of a problem-dependent geometric constant [MATH]. However, no means of bounding [MATH] from below as a function of the problem size has been available, and hence the number of iterations could not be given as an explicit function of the problem size. We therefore give, when the forward problem is an integer linear program (ILP), the number of iterations sufficient for projected subgradient descent applied to the suboptimality loss to achieve exact consistency with the observed data, as a fully explicit function of the number of samples, the dimension of the features, the ranges of the features, and the structure of the constraint coefficient matrix, up to polynomial factors in the basic constants (the diameter of the weight set, the step-size parameter, and the Lipschitz constant of the suboptimality loss).
tldr: This paper analyzes the iteration complexity of data-driven inverse optimization for integer linear programs, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper aims to provide explicit bounds on the number of iterations needed for exact inverse optimization of integer linear programs, a problem in operations research.
method: The authors apply projected subgradient descent to the suboptimality loss and derive explicit iteration bounds based on problem size parameters.
result: They obtain a fully explicit bound on the number of iterations sufficient for exact consistency, expressed in terms of sample size, feature dimension, and constraint matrix structure.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of inverse optimization but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Homogeneous Self-Dual Embedding Via Perspective Functions
authors: Goran Banjac
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a generalization of the well-known homogeneous self-dual embedding model, which is widely used in conic optimization. The new embedding applies to a problem of minimizing the sum of two proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions and can be represented as a single inequality that uses perspectives of these functions and of their conjugates. A solution to the proposed embedding encodes a primal-dual solution to the original problem when available, or an infeasibility certificate otherwise. We then use the Douglas-Rachford algorithm to find a solution to the embedding and discuss its efficient implementation by exploiting the problem structure. The resulting algorithm recovers an existing method for solving quadratic cone programs as a special case. We demonstrate the generality and effectiveness of the algorithm on a class of convex optimization problems with non-smooth objective function and non-conic constraints.
tldr: This paper presents a generalization of the homogeneous self-dual embedding model for convex optimization using perspective functions.
motivation: To extend the homogeneous self-dual embedding technique to a broader class of convex optimization problems involving non-smooth objectives and non-conic constraints.
method: The authors propose a new embedding that represents the optimization problem as a single inequality using perspectives of the objective functions and their conjugates, and solve it via the Douglas-Rachford algorithm.
result: The algorithm recovers existing methods for quadratic cone programs as a special case and demonstrates effectiveness on problems with non-smooth objectives and non-conic constraints.
conclusion: The proposed embedding and algorithm provide a unified framework for solving a wide class of convex optimization problems, including those with infeasibility certificates.

title: Nuancing The Unicity Of $q$-rationals
authors: Perrine Jouteur, Olga Paris-Romaskevich, Alexander Thomas
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove unicity of [MATH]-rational numbers up to conjugacy, using character varieties. Despite the unicity, we exhibit a two-parameter family of deformations of rationals with a modular symmetry. We prove that there are exactly two deformations which deliver the usual [MATH]-integers: the original [MATH]-rationals defined by Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko, and another new one. Although the new family can be obtained by conjugacy from the old one, new positivity properties appear. In addition, this new family provides a direct computation of the Jones polynomial of rational knots.
tldr: This paper studies the unicity and deformations of q-rational numbers using character varieties, with applications to knot theory.
motivation: To understand the structure of q-rational numbers and their deformations, and to connect them to knot invariants.
method: Uses character varieties to prove unicity and constructs a two-parameter family of deformations with modular symmetry.
result: Proves unicity of q-rationals up to conjugacy, exhibits two deformations yielding usual q-integers, and shows new positivity properties and direct computation of Jones polynomial.
conclusion: The new family of q-rationals provides a direct link to knot theory and exhibits novel positivity properties.

title: Langevin For Nonconvex Optimization: Exact, Inexact And Zeroth-Order
authors: Emanuele Naldi, Marco Rando, Lorenzo Rosasco, Silvia Villa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Langevin-based methods for non-convex optimization under smoothness and dissipativity assumptions. Our focus is on obtaining non-asymptotic bounds for the expected excess risk rather than sampling guarantees for the full target distribution. The key ingredient of our analysis is a direct passage from relative entropy to objective-value error, based on a weighted Csisz\'ar--Kullback--Pinsker inequality and exponential-moment estimates. This avoids intermediate Wasserstein bounds and yields sharper dependence on the Log-Sobolev constant, a quantity that may scale exponentially with the inverse temperature and the dimension in non-convex problems. We first analyze the Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm with exact gradients and derive explicit bounds on [MATH] in terms of the inverse temperature, dimension, stepsize, smoothness and dissipativity parameters, and the Log-Sobolev constant. We then extend the result to an inexact-gradient version of ULA, allowing for biased and stochastic gradient surrogates whose mean-square error grows at most quadratically in the state. This framework covers stochastic gradients and zeroth-order estimators based only on function evaluations. In particular, we show that both Gaussian and spherical finite-difference estimators fit into the inexact-ULA theory and obtain explicit function-evaluation complexity bounds for zeroth-order Langevin optimization. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first non-asymptotic global non-convex optimization complexity bounds for zeroth-order ULA. We also provide numerical experiments illustrating the behavior of the proposed zeroth-order Langevin schemes.
tldr: This paper studies Langevin-based methods for non-convex optimization, providing non-asymptotic bounds on expected excess risk using relative entropy techniques.
motivation: Non-convex optimization is important in machine learning, and Langevin algorithms offer a way to escape local minima, but existing analyses often rely on sampling guarantees or Wasserstein bounds that are suboptimal.
method: The authors use a weighted Csiszár–Kullback–Pinsker inequality and exponential-moment estimates to directly bound objective-value error from relative entropy, avoiding intermediate Wasserstein bounds. They analyze exact, inexact, and zeroth-order versions of the Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm.
result: They derive explicit bounds on expected excess risk in terms of inverse temperature, dimension, stepsize, smoothness, dissipativity, and Log-Sobolev constant. For zeroth-order ULA, they provide the first non-asymptotic global non-convex optimization complexity bounds.
conclusion: The proposed analysis yields sharper dependence on the Log-Sobolev constant and extends to stochastic and zeroth-order gradient estimators, demonstrating practical applicability.

title: Extremal Fences With Polyforms
authors: Alexis Langlois-R\'emillard, Mia N. M\"u{\ss}ig, \'erika Rold\'an
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present results around an isoperimetric problem built on polyforms: What is the biggest enclosed area one can build using polyforms in each of the three plane tessellations? We give challenges to the readers and present Shimauchi's proof of the biggest area a fence made of pentominoes can enclose. A translation of the instance using integer linear programming is also given. A companion web app is available to test some of the challenges we propose and for activities, and we included extra pages with a cutout handout of the board and pieces of the puzzles, so that you can print and cut them to read this paper hands on.
tldr: This paper studies an isoperimetric problem using polyforms in plane tessellations, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: To determine the maximum area that can be enclosed by a fence made of polyforms in each of the three plane tessellations.
method: The authors present challenges, provide Shimauchi's proof for pentominoes, and translate the problem into integer linear programming.
result: They give the biggest enclosed area for fences made of pentominoes and offer a companion web app and cutout handouts.
conclusion: The paper is a recreational mathematics puzzle with no relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fractional $\frac{1}{2}$-Laplacian Of Holomorphic Functions Via Jacobi Polynomials
authors: Fabrizio Colombo, Antonino de Martino, Alberto Debernardi Pinos
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a distributional definition of the [MATH]-fractional Laplacian for smooth functions with power-type singularities at the origin, including negative monomials and certain holomorphic functions with isolated singularities. The construction is based on a suitable space of test functions related to the Lizorkin space of test functions, for which both the test functions and their fractional Laplacians belong to the Schwarz class and vanish to infinite order at the origin, and thus compensate for any singularity of power type at the origin. This allows the [MATH]-fractional Laplacian to be defined by duality without requiring the underlying function to satisfy the usual integrability assumptions. The considered distributional framework is shown to be invariant under the [MATH]-fractional Laplacian, yielding a natural semigroup property. By applying the construction term by term to Laurent series we obtain new series that, remarkably, involve Jacobi polynomials. With this procedure we define the fractional Laplacian for a class of holomorphic functions and derive several applications, with particular emphasis on the recently developed theory of the quaternionic fine structures of the spectral theory on the [MATH]-spectrum, describing the functional calculi extending the classical holomorphic functional calculus in the various classes of holomorphic-type functions arising from the Fueter-Sce-Qian extension theorem.
tldr: This paper defines the fractional 1/2-Laplacian for holomorphic functions with singularities using a distributional framework and Jacobi polynomials, with applications to quaternionic spectral theory.
motivation: The fractional Laplacian is a key operator in analysis, but its definition for functions with power-type singularities is not straightforward. The authors aim to extend the definition to holomorphic functions with isolated singularities.
method: They construct a space of test functions (Lizorkin-type) that vanish to infinite order at the origin, allowing the fractional Laplacian to be defined by duality. The construction is applied term-by-term to Laurent series, yielding series involving Jacobi polynomials.
result: The distributional framework is invariant under the fractional Laplacian and satisfies a semigroup property. Explicit formulas for the fractional Laplacian of monomials and holomorphic functions are obtained.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous definition of the fractional 1/2-Laplacian for a class of holomorphic functions, with potential applications in quaternionic spectral theory and functional calculi.

title: Data Driven Modeling Of Nonlinear Dynamics In A Rotating Detonation Combustor Via Finite Dimensional Approximations Of The Koopman Operator
authors: David Oexle, Tobias Breiten, Myles D. Bohon
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Rotating Detonation Combustor (RDC) is a promising technology for increasing efficiency in propulsion and power generation applications. The dynamics of the RDC are governed by continuously propagating detonation waves within an annular combustion chamber. Multiple operating modes can be observed, including nonlinear interactions between counter-rotating waves and the emergence of standing wave patterns. Koopman operator theory provides a framework to globally linearize nonlinear dynamical systems by representing their evolution in the space of observables rather than states. In this work, finite-dimensional approximations of the Koopman operator are constructed using variants of Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) applied to high-speed video data capturing the natural flame luminosity of the detonation waves in the RDC at the Technical University (TU) Berlin. By introducing time-delay embeddings as a dictionary of observables, this approach overcomes the limitations of standard DMD methods, particularly for accurate reconstruction of standing wave patterns and for capturing nonlinear interactions. In addition, a technique is presented to mitigate the influence of sensor noise in the luminosity measurements. Finally, it is shown that the DMD-based models provide insight into the dynamics of different operating modes by decomposing the reconstructed signal into its characteristic features.
tldr: This paper applies Koopman operator theory and dynamic mode decomposition to model nonlinear dynamics in a rotating detonation combustor.
motivation: Rotating detonation combustors are promising for propulsion efficiency, but their nonlinear dynamics are complex and need accurate modeling.
method: Finite-dimensional approximations of the Koopman operator are constructed using variants of Dynamic Mode Decomposition with time-delay embeddings on high-speed video data.
result: The DMD-based models accurately reconstruct standing wave patterns and capture nonlinear interactions, with a technique to mitigate sensor noise.
conclusion: The approach provides insight into different operating modes by decomposing the signal into characteristic features.

title: ReLU$^k$ Neural De Rham Complexes
